name: Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) Race Condition
principle: The product checks a resource state or identity, then later uses the resource through a reference that can change. An attacker can alter the resource between check and use, invalidating the check and causing unauthorized or unexpected actions.
detection_signals: C/C++ access(path, mode) or faccessat(path, mode) followed by fopen(path, ...), open(path, ...), unlink(path), chmod(path), chown(path), or rename(path, ...)
C/C++ stat(path, &st) or lstat(path, &st) followed by open(path, ...), fopen(path, ...), remove(path), or update using the same pathname
C/C++ realpath(path, ...) or readlink(path, ...) followed by file operation on the pathname without holding a file descriptor or lock
C/C++ setuid/setgid privileged code checks user permission on pathname, then performs privileged fopen/open/write on the same pathname

Java Files.exists(path), Files.isRegularFile(path), Files.isWritable(path), or Files.getOwner(path) followed by Files.newInputStream(path), Files.newOutputStream(path), Files.delete(path), or FileOutputStream(path)
Java File.exists(), File.canWrite(), File.isFile(), or File.getCanonicalPath() followed by FileInputStream, FileOutputStream, RandomAccessFile, delete(), or renameTo()
Shared variable or object state checked outside mutex/synchronized/Lock and then used later outside the same critical section
negative_signals: Check and use are both inside the same pthread_mutex_lock/pthread_mutex_unlock, synchronized block, ReentrantLock lock/unlock, or FileChannel.lock region
Code opens the resource first and performs fstat(fd, ...), fchmod(fd, ...), fchown(fd, ...), read/write on the same fd instead of reusing the pathname
open(path, O_CREAT|O_EXCL, ...) or openat(dirfd, name, O_NOFOLLOW, ...) is used for the security-sensitive operation
Privileged code drops effective uid/gid before open/fopen and performs the operation with the caller's privileges
Resource identity is revalidated immediately before use by comparing dev/inode from stat(path) with fstat(fd)
false_defense_traps: access(path, W_OK) before fopen(path, "w+") still races on the pathname
stat/lstat check before open does not bind the later open to the checked object
realpath(), getCanonicalPath(), or readlink() before use can be invalidated by rename or symlink replacement
Reducing delay between check and use only narrows the race window
Locking after the check does not protect the checked state
verification_focus: Can an attacker change the resource identity or state between the observed check API and the later use API?

consequence_chains.trigger: Shared resource is checked and then used without synchronization or atomicity
consequence_chains.consequence: Unexpected state, unauthorized resource access, or invalid execution logic

consequence_chains.trigger: Attacker replaces checked pathname with a symbolic link before use
consequence_chains.consequence: Operation follows link to an unintended file, enabling unauthorized read/write/delete

patch_principle: Avoid separate pre-checks; perform the intended operation atomically and handle failure from the use call.
Use file descriptors or handles: open once, then use fstat/fchmod/fchown/read/write on the same handle.
Acquire locks before the check and hold them through the use when sharing resources across processes or threads.
Use safe open flags and APIs such as O_NOFOLLOW, O_EXCL, openat with trusted dirfd, and FileChannel.lock where appropriate.
Drop effective uid/gid before file operations performed on behalf of an unprivileged user.

minimal_examples.safe: int fd = open(file, O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_NOFOLLOW, 0600);
